title: Homomorphic Aggregation of Continuous-Variable GKP States
abstract: Aggregating logical quantum information encoded in continuous-variable phase space is essential for distributed quantum computing. However, passive linear optics fail for non-Gaussian Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes due to symplectic lattice compression and entanglement-induced decoherence. We present an active, measurement-based framework for the homomorphic aggregation of multi-node GKP states. Utilizing GKP Bell states and homodyne feed-forward, we construct a completely positive trace-preserving map that computes the logical sum of distributed states while preserving the logical code space geometry up to correctable finite-squeezing deformations. We prove this protocol operates as an approximate quantum non-demolition measurement, bound its cryptographic leakage for continuous one-time pads, and derive analytical logical fidelity limits under finite-squeezing constraints.
summary: This paper presents an active, measurement-based protocol for homomorphically aggregating logical information encoded in CV GKP states. It proves that passive optical methods fail due to lattice compression and introduces a solution using homodyne measurements and feed-forward control. The result is crucial for scalable distributed quantum computing networks.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a method for homomorphically aggregating logical quantum information encoded in continuous-variable (CV) Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states across multiple distributed nodes.
main_result: An active, measurement-based framework utilizing GKP Bell states and homodyne feed-forward successfully computes the logical sum while preserving code space geometry up to correctable deformations.
method: The authors propose a Completely Positive Trace-Preserving (CPTP) map that bypasses the limitations of passive linear optics by incorporating active syndrome extraction and classical feed-forward displacement.
model_or_system: The system uses CV GKP states, which encode discrete logical information into an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space via a phase-space lattice. The process is analyzed within a measurement-based quantum computing (MBQC) framework.

main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the ability to perform intermediate syndrome extraction at network vertices to reset physical noise accumulation, and it operates within a finite-energy GKP subspace.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate performance scaling under various conditions: (a) linear cascade vs. logarithmic tree topology for variance ($\sigma_{	ext{out}}$); (b) logical fidelity convergence; and (c)-(f) the impact of physical channel attenuation ($\eta < 1$) on achievable fidelity.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the failure modes of passive optics due to lattice compression. It then introduces the active, measurement-based protocol using GKP Bell states and homodyne measurements. Finally, it derives analytical bounds on fidelity and security, showing that logarithmic tree routing is necessary for scalability.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical blueprint for scaling quantum computation beyond simple linear chains by addressing topological aggregation challenges inherent to continuous-variable encoding schemes.
